mainEntity.name: What is stablecoin PR and who is it for?

acceptedAnswer.text: Stablecoin PR is the communications strategy that builds and protects trust for a stablecoin issuer with journalists, regulators, exchange BD teams and liquidity providers. It is for founders launching a new stablecoin, teams preparing for MiCA or VARA compliance disclosures, and issuers whose existing narrative has been damaged by a depeg or audit delay. The core motion is reserve-first: every earned media placement leads with proof of reserves, auditor name and redemption mechanism before any yield or utility claim.

mainEntity.name: How much does stablecoin PR cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A fractional senior operator runs stablecoin PR for $5K–$12K/month, which covers narrative development, ongoing media relations and regulatory milestone coverage. A full launch sprint, covering the period from embargo prep through the first 30 days of coverage, runs $15K–$40K. Generalist agencies charge $15K–$45K/month for a model that staffs junior account executives on your project.

Tier-1 crypto with dedicated stablecoin coverage: CoinDesk, The Block, Blockworks, Cointelegraph and Decrypt. Mainstream financial press where the regulatory angle warrants it: Bloomberg, Financial Times, Reuters and Forbes. For regional distribution: BloomingBit and TokenPost in Korea, CoinPost and CryptoTimes JP in Japan, Inc42 in India, The National and Arabian Business in the Gulf. Outlet selection depends on a real news hook tied to reserves, regulation or adoption, not a wire blast.

mainEntity.name: How long does stablecoin PR take to show results?

acceptedAnswer.text: The highest-leverage window is the six to twelve weeks before a public launch moment. In that window, embargo relationships are built, the regulatory narrative is stress-tested and the attestation documentation is prepared in journalist-readable form. A well-prepared launch can deliver tier-1 placements on day one, as the RARI Chain launch demonstrated with 11 placements in 24 hours. Sustained coverage compounds from there with monthly attestation milestones and regulatory progress updates.
